title: candidate feedback draft - Evan Ross - SRE
strengths: Fast, methodical debugger - reproduces issues quickly and uses logs effectively
Clear communicator under pressure, good call-routing examples
concerns: Limited experience with distributed tracing platforms (only small PoC on Jaeger)
Hasn't run large-scale rollout pipelines (no experience with canary tooling at scale)
Some gaps on disaster recovery planning and SLO derivation
suggested_next_steps: Team match interview with current oncall rotation lead (focus: runbooks + incident postmortem)
Reference check (previous manager about ownership of oncall)
Optional short take-home on designing a DR plan for a stateful service
notes:
Quick notes from debrief: Evan is bright and pragmatic. Started at a mid-size infra company, primarily focused on core infra (monitoring + incident response). In the systems design section he tended to favor pragmatic tradeoffs, but struggled a bit to articulate how to scale a multi-region control plane under network partitions - asked follow-ups but his answers stayed high-level.

Debugging exercise: walked through a CPU spike on a host; used top/strace/lsof appropriately, hypothesized a runaway cron job, validated with process tree. Good troubleshooting flow.

Oncall & Ops: he described owning pager rotations, writes good runbooks (shared examples), but hasn't led a major incident review that changed company-wide policy. Experience mostly at ~200 node fleets, not 10k+.

Culture fit: collaborative, takes feedback well. Showed curiosity about telemetry and cost optimization.

Open questions / TODOs: reach out to Priya to confirm scale of infra at last company (nodes, services). Ask candidate for specific runbook link he mentioned (dev wrote a sample but didn't paste). Decide if we want the extra take-home coding/design task or rely on team match.

This is a draft for the hiring packet. Will iterate after reference check and team-match.
